PART A   /   1 OF 5

How it works

How do 36 Aeroleafs turn at different speeds and still supply one electrical output? Follow the wind through one rotor, then see where the outputs meet.

Engineering schematics · illustrative motion and signals

  1. Incoming wind energy

    Pwind = ½ρAv³

    Double the wind speed from 3 to 6 m/s and eight times as much power flows through the same swept area at the same air density. This makes the wind speed at each rotor crucial to the waterfront study.

  2. Rotor capture

    Why design for a light breeze?

    Each vertical-axis rotor accepts wind from any horizontal direction. Its curved blades occupy a large fraction of the swept area. This high solidity helps the wind produce starting torque. The manufacturer gives a starting threshold of 2.5 m/s.

    The rotor captures only part of the available power. The ideal Betz limit is 16/27 (59.3%). Drag on the returning blade and disturbed airflow reduce real capture. In a simulation at 7 m/s, one baseline Aeroleaf rotor reached a peak power coefficient of 0.107 when its blade tips moved at half the wind speed. Aeroleaf rotor study, Fig. 12

  3. Shaft work

    Pshaft = torque × angular velocity

    Wind pushes harder on one side of the rotor than the other, creating torque on the shaft. At a given mechanical power, a slower shaft must carry more torque. The shaft drives the generator directly.

  4. Generation

    One permanent-magnet generator per Aeroleaf

    Magnets rotate past stationary copper coils and induce alternating current (AC). Direct drive eliminates the gearbox, and the permanent magnets supply the magnetic field without brushes. As the rotor speeds up, the AC frequency and voltage change. The manufacturer lists 170 V AC at 850 rpm for the 300 W generator. New World Wind 36A data sheet

  5. Conversion and grid connection

    Variable AC → shared 48 V DC bus → grid AC

    Electronics in each Aeroleaf rectify its AC output. The 36 modules feed a common direct-current bus in parallel, so each rotor can follow its own gusts. The inverter then supplies AC at the voltage and frequency required for grid connection.

    The shared bus and inverter are critical to delivery. A fault in either can interrupt the whole tree’s output. At 48 V, a given power requires more current than at a higher voltage, so cable sizing matters for limiting resistive losses.

How much of the wind reaches the grid?

Overall efficiency = capture efficiency × generator efficiency × delivery efficiency

Each stage passes on a fraction of the power it receives. We now turn to the Aeroleaf itself. Why did we choose two curved blades, and what material suits the Hong Kong waterfront?

PART B   /   2 OF 5

The Aeroleaf

Choosing the rotor geometry

For our Hong Kong design, we use a two-blade, single-stage Savonius rotor with semicircular buckets. The dimensions below describe this proposed geometry.

Two blades
Adding blades can increase turning torque, but also increases drag on the returning side. The team selected two blades to balance starting torque and power capture.
Semicircular buckets
The simple cross-section makes tooling and fabrication easier to estimate.
One stage
Stacking stages can smooth torque over a revolution. A single stage keeps the leaf silhouette and simplifies the assembly.

Dimensions of the proposed rotor

0.60 m × 1.00 m
Rotor diameter × height in the team’s design.
H/D = 1.67
Height divided by diameter. The proposed proportions balance swept area with the loads on the support.
Dₑ/D ≈ 1
The endplate is about as wide as the rotor. A larger plate can retain more airflow but adds inertia at startup.

Blade material for the waterfront

We propose glass-fibre-reinforced plastic (GFRP). It can be moulded into curved blades, keeps rotating mass low and resists corrosion in humid, salty air. UV protection, joint inspections and typhoon load checks are part of the proposed site design.

From one rotor to the 36A

36 rotors
On a shared frame, rotor spacing affects wake interference, wind loading and material demand over the life cycle.
10.8 kW installed
36 Aeroleaf modules × 300 W. Actual generation depends on the wind reaching each module.
9.8 m tall
The tree’s height makes nearby buildings, trees and lighting columns relevant to wind exposure. Overturning loads and salt-spray exposure need a site assessment.

These whole-tree specifications provide the commercial baseline for the site comparison. WindTree 36A technical data sheet

Site Selection

How different are urban and exposed winds?

9.9 km/hHKO Headquarters
22.9 km/hWaglan Island

Long-term annual means show how much exposure matters. We screened three sites for wind, local demand and practical access.

Hong Kong Observatory · 1991–2020 normals, Table 7

Three sites for one demonstration

Site A. Kai Tak Runway Park

3.65 / 5

A 2.82-hectare waterfront park with a large lawn, 24-hour opening and real lighting demand, but weak wind.

Site B. Belcher Bay Promenade in Kennedy Town

4.45 / 5

A busy urban waterfront on Hong Kong Island West, with an 5.8 m/s wind, and a genuine night-time lighting load.

Site C. Tai Mo Shan

3.85 / 5

the Tai Mo Shan summit. The strongest onshore wind resource, but no local load, difficult access, and country-park approval required.

Belcher Bay · proposed pilot site

The group scores this site highest for its combination of wind exposure, local use and access. The project models 4,320 kWh/year for one tree (36 modules × 120 kWh/year).

The yield scenario uses the Green Island reference of 5.8 m/s. Wind at turbine height on the promenade still needs to be measured.

Cost & Carbon

What would one WindTree cost at Belcher Bay, and what could it return to the buyer and the grid?

Purchase and upkeep

Equipment starting price
HK$450,000
Routine maintenance per year
HK$3,000

Rounded budget estimates for one tree. Freight, site works and installation require a separate allowance.

Feed-in tariff

Annual tariff receipts
HK$13,000
After routine maintenance
HK$10,000 / year

If HK Electric approves the application, the model values 4,320 kWh/year at HK$3/kWh through the scheme’s 2033 endpoint. The operating contribution is before tax and other costs.

Profits tax deduction

Illustrative purchase-year tax saving
HK$37,000 or
HK$74,000

A qualifying company could deduct eligible equipment expenditure from taxable profits. The saving depends on available taxable profits and the applicable tax rate.

What about carbon?

≈ 2.5 t CO₂e / year

Estimated grid-level displacement at 4,320 kWh/year, using HK Electric’s 2025 average of 0.59 kg CO₂e/kWh. Under the assumed tariff agreement, HK Electric receives the environmental attributes.

≈ 8 years

Illustrative carbon payback using the embodied emissions of a comparable wind tree. Lower generation would extend the time needed to offset those emissions.

Calculation basis and assumptions

  • C’s scenario uses the 5.8 m/s reference and assumes that 4,320 kWh reaches the meter each year. Wind measurements at the proposed site are still needed.
  • HK$449,100 equipment estimate at the assumed exchange rate. Annual receipts of HK$12,960 less HK$2,948.40 in routine maintenance give HK$10,011.60 before tax and other costs.
  • Assuming the full equipment cost qualifies and sufficient profits fall in one tax band, HK$449,100 × 8.25% or 16.5% gives a one-off saving of about HK$37,051 or HK$74,102.
  • 4,320 × 0.59 = 2,548.8 kg CO₂e per year. Dividing the comparator footprint of 19.98–20.85 t CO₂e by 2.5488 t/year gives 7.8–8.2 years.

Source: Part D, WindTree 36A Economic Analysis (V2) and presentation script. Carbon comparator: Ngoc et al., 2022.

Part E · Public pilot

Why trial one tree?

At Belcher Bay, how much electricity could a small wind turbine deliver over four seasons? A single monitored tree could give Hong Kong a public record of what happens on the waterfront.

Equipment starting price
HK$450,000

Before installation. Electricity sales alone are unlikely to cover the investment.

Annual generation forecast
4,320 kWh

Our estimate for one 36A. Wind at the proposed location still needs to be measured.

Measure the wind first. If the readings support the forecast, monitor one tree for a full year and compare its metered output with the estimate.

Public access to the data ↓
Part E · Public pilot

What would residents gain?

A QR code beside the tree would open a public webpage. Readings would upload automatically, so residents could check the wind on the promenade and revisit the same page from home.

Quarterly public report ↓
Part E · Public pilot

If generation falls short

Was it a calm quarter, or was the tree out of service on windy days?

Each quarter, the operator would submit the records and the responsible department would publish the findings.

Group conclusion ↓
WindTree at Belcher Bay · Hong Kong feasibility study

Conclusion

Belcher Bay ranked first among the three sites we studied.

Financial returns are limited. We would trial one tree if local wind measurements support the forecast and an operator can fund and maintain it.

After one year · Use the public operating record to decide whether to continue, adjust or end the trial.

Part E · Q&A

Promenade access

Could the tree or people stopping to scan its QR code block the promenade?

We would survey the site with the promenade operator. The layout needs room to stop outside the main path and a clear route for maintenance crews. If the space is too narrow, we would move the proposed installation.
